sources.own_observation: The selected corridor remains in the same trunk through lower widenings and the coastal gorge to South Bay.

correspondence.finding: The southeastern chosen opening enters a west-trending high valley with a broad pale channel belt and short lateral ravines. The original image covers the opening and every stored short segment in this upper approach. Fabbroni’s study-area outline and prose place the Tocomar–Campo Amarillo landscape here; they do not individually name each small feeder.

The westward corridor bends northwest within a widening alluvial trough, accepting lateral valley and fan arrivals before approaching the Olacapato-side plain. A narrow damp/vegetated-looking channel belt and wider dry washes occur in the same trough. The botanical study describes Río Tocomar traversing Campo Amarillo toward Cauchari.

The lower upper-valley approach spreads over a broad fan beside a solar-array-like development and enters the pale southern Cauchari margin. The selected turn north is covered continuously at regional scale. No exact current wetted thread, infrastructure operation or scalar river name across the fan is asserted.

The selected northward continuation remains in the long Cauchari saline depression, beside successive eastern alluvial fans and western mountain margins. Pale salt crust, darker sinuous floor traces and fan tongues remain within the same southern receiving setting. No separate river channel is required across this salt floor.

The northern Cauchari continuation reaches broad salt crust and the margin of an extensive rectangular evaporation-pond complex. The approach remains geographically inside the southern salar; this observation does not establish a hydraulic route through the pond embankments or into Olaroz.

The selection passes through the narrowed zone between Cauchari and Olaroz, near the east edge of the broad western Archibarca fan, a road-like crossing and large evaporation ponds. The inventory independently classifies two salar nuclei and describes the fan as a barrier. The images expose the setting but do not establish the selected through-connection across this intervening zone.

North of the intervening neck, the selected continuation turns over the broad Olaroz salt floor, passes east of the curved evaporation-pond complex and ends within the interior saline receiving setting. This actual modeled endpoint is geographically covered, independently of the unresolved southern inter-salar transfer. A river line across the playa is neither required nor inferred.

The chosen opening corresponds to the southern portion of an elongated lake and the adjoining north-south lake/valley setting. The lake, neighbouring smaller waterbodies and local drainage mouths are directly visible. This establishes the opening location only; the required onward eastward transfer is assessed separately.

The selected course turns east from the western lake-country valley and then southeast across a ridged upland containing numerous ponds and incised drainage lines. Both the lake-side exits and several eastern channels are visible. The inspected overview, upper detail and focused opening detail do not establish one through-going connection that links the chosen lake exit, these successive selected upper intervals and the eastern collector. Some channels lie along alternative routes. The finding does not declare those alternatives equivalent to the selected passage or infer a connection merely from proximity.

At the eastern side of the upper terrain, the selected corridor turns north into a broad alluvial river valley. Its channel, meanders, gravelly or pale alluvial surfaces and lateral drainage arrivals are visible. This component establishes the northward collector setting, without resolving the missing upstream transfer.

The northward collector continues through a broad meandering and locally braided valley, with several lateral stream arrivals and nearby elongated ponds or waterbodies. The successive selected pieces correspond to this same connected valley at ordinary corridor scale. No individual side-lake or tributary name is assigned.

The corridor continues north and northeast through alternating wider alluvial sections and narrower reaches. Elongated lakes and small ponds border the valley. The imagery supplies continuous valley correspondence and the downstream continuation; adjacent lake surfaces are not all presumed to be river reaches merely because the generalized selected line passes near their margins.

A continuous northeast-trending channel valley runs toward the coast, with a meandering lower section, numerous short lateral gullies and lower alluvial surfaces. The selected line generalizes bends within this drainage setting. The local lake labels, exact banks and present flow conditions remain unassigned.

The observed river valley reaches the west side of Hadley Bay through a low coastal alluvial outlet. Imagery establishes the actual valley-to-shore connection and adjacent open receiving water. The simplified selected endpoint is treated at coastal-corridor scale; an exact river-mouth or shoreline vertex is not asserted. Retained ARC403 independently identifies Hadley Bay and describes its long southward reach and surrounding shores.

correspondence.component_scope: Chosen northwestern feeder and Pleasant Lake entry
correspondence.finding: The chosen opening lies in the small, connected wooded stream valley northwest of Pleasant Lake. Detailed cartography shows converging unnamed feeder channels and the wetland-fringed collecting stream entering the lake. The selected opening and lake entry correspond at ordinary corridor scale. No separate feeder hydronym was established.

correspondence.component_scope: Pleasant Lake outlet, Scraggly Lake and Junior Lake join
correspondence.finding: The detailed original depicts the short outlet from the south side of Pleasant Lake into the eastern arm of Scraggly Lake, the connected Scraggly water body and its western narrow connection with Junior Lake. The selected lake chain is continuous; nearby Shaw Lake is a separate side-lake connection.

correspondence.component_scope: Junior Lake passage and West Grand Lake entrance
correspondence.finding: Junior Lake continues south through the mapped connected narrows and Junior Bay into West Grand Lake. The selected passage stays within this lake-and-strait chain, distinct from the nearby Sysladobsis and Pocumcus lake arms.

correspondence.component_scope: West Grand Lake outlet and Grand Lake Stream to Big Lake
correspondence.finding: The lake original follows the selected West Grand Lake passage to its southeastern outlet and the distinctly labelled Grand Lake Stream through the settlement, falls and outlet channel to Big Lake. The Waterway Commission identifies West Grand Lake dam as the control on this stream. No current discharge or operating condition is inferred.

correspondence.component_scope: Big Lake, Long Lake and Lewey Lake through Princeton
correspondence.finding: The mapped water-body chain carries the selection northeast across Big Lake, through its connected Long Lake and Lewey Lake setting and the Princeton narrows into the western Grand Falls impoundment. The Waterway Commission expressly identifies Big, Long and Lewey lakes with the West Branch St. Croix. Intervening channels and the Princeton passage are visible; the lake names remain component names.

correspondence.component_scope: Grand Falls Flowage, main-river join and Kellyland outlet setting
correspondence.finding: Original cartography shows the connected western impoundment approaching Grand Falls, its join with the incoming St. Croix and the downstream Kellyland corridor. The commissioned study describes Grand Falls Flowage as interconnected western-branch waters and distinguishes the dam outlet from the separate powerhouse conveyance channel. Both belong to the same receiving river system; no precise facility passage is assigned to a generalized position.

correspondence.component_scope: Grand Falls–Woodland Flowage–lower St. Croix corridor
correspondence.finding: The lower original continuously depicts St. Croix River from Kellyland into the elongated Woodland impoundment, through the Woodland dam setting and onward toward Baring. The study independently identifies the connected Grand Falls and Woodland receiving reaches. All three selected parts are considered as the generalized lower-river corridor; straight positions are not asserted to be surveyed channel or bank traces.

correspondence.component_scope: Baring bend and the next lower-river join
correspondence.finding: The detailed map depicts the continuous St. Croix bend at Baring, its receiving side streams and the continuation toward Milltown. This short selected fragment and its joins with the preceding and following generalized fragments remain within the same connected lower receiving corridor.

correspondence.component_scope: Milltown–Calais/St. Stephen and actual estuarine ending
correspondence.finding: The lower original establishes the St. Croix continuation through the Milltown and Calais/St. Stephen corridor into widened tidal water. The selected ending lies in the connected northern estuarine embayment east of Calais; the map shows that embayment joining the wider St. Croix estuary. This is the actual selected receiving setting, not an extension of the finding to the farther mouth at Passamaquoddy Bay.

correspondence.component_scope: chosen headward opening and upper mainstem
correspondence.finding: The chosen northern opening lies in a visible southward upland stream valley. Its initial tributary joins and southwestward turn remain within the same connected valley corridor. The selected short intermediate part is a generalized connector within this river setting, not evidence of a separately named lake.

The western upper valley continues south, receives visible side tributaries, bends southeast and passes the broadened channel around the short straight selected connector. The adjacent dark waterbody east of the valley is not used to assign a lake name or infer an off-course connection. Small cloud patches affect individual pixels, but the same narrow valley and its entering and leaving channel are evident at ordinary corridor scale.

The southward valley turns southeast into a broader river corridor, with visible side-stream joins and gravelly/braided channel sections. It reaches the substantial north-to-south eastern tributary junction before continuing south. The independently authored Bird map depicts the corresponding western arm joining the Kirchoffer River trunk.

correspondence.component_scope: middle to lower mainstem and tributary joins
correspondence.finding: The selected southern continuation below the major junction follows a single evident trunk valley. Further western and eastern feeders join it before its southeastward bend. The image pair overlaps across these joins; no isolated pond, parallel valley or unsupported cross-divide transfer is used.

correspondence.component_scope: lower mainstem widened channel and gorge approach
correspondence.finding: The lower river continues through bends, channel islands and broad dark-water reaches, receives the eastern tributary and enters the longer southward gorge. Nearby ponds and wet lowland patches are distinguishable from the selected through-course. No separate lake hydronym is established for the river widenings. Bird describes the named Kirchoffer lower course crossing the South Bay Lowland and approaching the sea in a gorge.

The final selected part remains in the southward gorge and reaches the coastal mouth at South Bay. The river exits through the narrow lower valley into the same visible bay-margin tidal receiving setting. Bird’s own Figure11 labels Kirchoffer River at this South Bay coast west of Coral Harbour, and the authorial mouth account independently describes a gorge with cliffed sides. This is correspondence of the actual ending, not assignment from a nearby river label alone.
